newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December T-bonds finish up strongly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December T-bonds finish up strongly.

text.p: U.S. December Treasury bonds ended near a nine-month high after an afternoon of brisk dealer buying that shored up technical optimism.
December pushed as high as 115-11/32 late in the day, buoyed by the aggressive dealer buying. One Wall Street firm reportedly bought 8,000 to 10,000 December contracts, traders said.

The contract had languished in negative ground much of the morning, pressured by profit-taking from recent gains. But midday talk of a cash buyer of two-year notes pushed Dec through 114-25/32 and technicals extended gains, traders said.
Traders noted heavy volume on the rally.
"There were some big buyers, but fundamentally I don't know," one T-bond futures trader said. "We really acted blah on the numbers and then we just had the heavy flows," he said.
The long end chopped around briefly then headed lower after an early batch of U.S. economic data.
October consumer prices were reported exactly in line with Wall Street's forecast at up 0.3 percent overall and up 0.2 percent excluding food and energy.
October retail sales rose 0.2 percent overall and 0.4 percent excluding autos, versus forecasts for up 0.3 in both.
One trader said the strong close sets December up for more gains on Friday. He said technical momentum could take the contract as high as 116-00.
Others said the market was vulnerable to profit-taking before the weekend.
Industrial production and capacity utilization figures for October will be released at 0815 CST/1415 GMT on Friday. Output was forecast to be unchanged with capacity use at 83.0 percent.
December T-bond and note options expire at midday on Friday.

December T-bonds settled up 18/32 in a range from 114-12/32 to 115-11/32, December 10-year notes closed up 10/32 to 110-27/32, December muni-bonds rallied 18/32 to 117-13/32 and March Euros finished up three basis points at 94.49.
